Write a dataset to a store

Source: R/write.R
store_write.Rd

Writes a table, an sf object or a terra::SpatRaster as one dataset of the store, in the primary location and in every available secondary one. The files are staged locally, checked, uploaded where they are missing, verified by MD5, and the catalogs of each location are switched to the new version last, so that readers always see either the old or the new version.

Usage

store_write(
  st,
  x,
  dataset,
  title,
  description,
  key = NULL,
  partition = NULL,
  mode = c("create", "replace", "update"),
  h3_res = 5L,
  geocode = TRUE,
  geocode_engine = c("auto", "s2", "planar"),
  max_files = 50L,
  history = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  inputs = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  rows_per_group = 50000L,
  crs = NULL,
  datatype = NULL,
  nodata = NULL,
  gdal = NULL
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect(). It is updated in place, so that it can be used for further writes without refreshing.

x

The data: a data frame, an sf object, a terra::SpatRaster, or a lazy table on a DuckDB connection (see "DuckDB input").

dataset

The dataset's full name: lower-case letters, digits and _, with / between folders, e.g. "sales/daily".

title, description

Short title and description, required.

key

Columns that identify the rows, or NULL. Their values must be unique together.

partition

NULL for one file; column names to write one file per combination of their values; or "h3" (geospatial data) to partition by the H3 parent cell at the finest resolution that gives at most max_files files. The catalog records which of the two it was. On update, leave it out or give what was given on create (see "Modes").

mode

"create", "replace" or "update" (see "Modes").

h3_res

H3 resolution of the geocodes, 0 to 15.

geocode

FALSE writes geospatial data without H3 cells and without index table (no engine is recorded); spatial reads then use bounding boxes only.

geocode_engine

"auto", "s2" or "planar": how the H3 cells of geometries that cross cell edges are computed (see "Geocoding engines"); recorded with the dataset. An update uses the stored engine (a different one aborts); a dataset written without one geocodes new rows with "s2". Rows geocoded in the plane ("planar", or the fallback of "auto") that are invalid in the plane too (for example a self-intersecting ring) are first repaired with sf::st_make_valid(), silently: the repaired copy is used only for the cells, and keeps only the parts of the row's own dimension (none: no cells, h3 is NA). The stored geometry is unchanged.

max_files

Most partition files.

history

TRUE or FALSE sets the dataset's history setting; NULL leaves it as it is.

source, inputs

Optional provenance: where the data come from and what they were made from.

columns

Named character vector, column (or layer) name to description. NULL keeps the descriptions already stored for columns that still exist.

check

TRUE compares sampled rows of the staged files with x before anything is uploaded (see store_check()).

rows_per_group

Rows per Parquet row group.

crs

The coordinate reference system of the column geometry of a lazy DuckDB table (anything sf::st_crs() accepts, e.g. 4326); required for such a table, ignored otherwise (an sf object carries its own).

datatype

For a raster: the data type of the file, one for all layers. NULL (the default) keeps the type of the file the raster was read from; a raster that is not read from a file gets the smallest integer type that holds its values when they are whole numbers, else "FLT8S". Or one of "INT1U", "INT2U", "INT2S", "INT4U", "INT4S", "FLT4S", "FLT8S"; the write aborts when the values do not fit an integer type given. See "Rasters". Aborts for any other data.

nodata

For a raster: the one number that marks missing cells in the file. Cells holding it are missing when read back, so nodata = 0 declares that 0 is not a value of the map. NULL (the default) uses, in this order: a flag set with terra::NAflag(x) <- on a raster read from files (a raster in memory keeps no flag: its cells become missing at once); the NoData tag of the source file; for an integer type its default (255 for INT1U, 65535 for INT2U, -32768 for INT2S, 4294967295 for INT4U, -2147483648 for INT4S), which a type kept from the file or given with datatype gets only when cells are missing; none for a float type, whose missing cells are NaN. A Byte file without a tag whose 0 means "outside the map" therefore gets no NoData value unless nodata = 0 is given. See "Rasters". Aborts for any other data.

gdal

For a raster: NULL, or a character vector of KEY=VALUE creation options of GDAL's COG driver, e.g. c("COMPRESS=ZSTD", "LEVEL=9"). An option replaces the default of the same key (COMPRESS=DEFLATE, PREDICTOR=2 or 3, BLOCKSIZE=512, BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER, OVERVIEWS=IGNORE_EXISTING, OVERVIEW_RESAMPLING=NEAREST or AVERAGE); other options are added. See "Rasters". Aborts for any other data.

Value

A tibble with one row per location, invisibly: location, role, status ("written", "unchanged", "same" for a secondary that already held the version, "behind" or "unavailable"), files (files of the version), uploaded (files sent), bytes (bytes sent) and seconds. The attribute version holds the dataset's version.

Kinds

The kind is set by the class of x: an sf object is geospatial, a SpatRaster is a raster, any other data frame is a table.

  • Geospatial data get the columns .rcs_id (row identifier), h3 (the H3 cell at h3_res holding the largest part of each geometry; not with geocode = FALSE) and bbox (bounding box), and are sorted by h3. Rows that cross H3 cells are listed in an index table <dataset>__h3, written, replaced and removed with the dataset.

  • Prepared geospatial data (rcs_geo_add(), or rows read back with collect()) may hold these columns already: .rcs_id is dropped and assigned again; h3 and bbox must equal what the write computes (else the write aborts naming the rows; prepare with the same geocode_engine, or call rcs_geo_strip() first), and h3_res, when not given, is taken from the cells. Columns h3_p<r> are written as they are; with partition = "h3" one named as the chosen partition column must hold the same cells, and then serves as it. Raw and prepared data give the same version.

  • A raster is written as one Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG), the only raster format; it cannot be partitioned or updated (see "Rasters").

  • A lazy table on a DuckDB connection is a table, or geospatial when it has a column geometry (see "DuckDB input").

Rasters

A SpatRaster is written as one Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG), the only raster format: a reader can fetch a part of it without the rest, also from a bucket. The raster needs a CRS, cell values and unique layer names.

What is stored where. The file holds the cell values only; for a class map, the codes. What describes them is recorded per layer in the catalog and in the dataset's manifest: the data type, the NoData value (nodata), the resolution and the dimensions (resolution, dim), the legend of a categorical layer (values, levels, levels_name) and its colours (color_values, colors). store_read() returns the raster with its categories and colours set again, and store_describe() shows the record. No side file (.aux.xml, .aux.json) is written.

  • Data type (datatype). All layers get one type, as a GeoTIFF requires. With datatype = NULL, the first rule that applies:

    1. A raster read from files, with its cells still on disk, keeps the type of its source: a Byte map stays INT1U, an FLT4S file stays FLT4S. No pass over the cells is needed. This rule is skipped when the layers have different types, and for a raster with a scale or an offset (in the file, or set with terra::scoff()), whose values are not the stored numbers.

    2. Whole numbers get the smallest of INT1U, INT2U, INT2S, INT4U, INT4S that holds the values and the NoData value: codes 1 to 5 with nodata = 0 take one byte per cell. Whole numbers are integer layers (terra::is.int()) and categorical layers; doubles that happen to be whole are not, so convert them with terra::as.int() first.

    3. Anything else is FLT8S. Doubles are never narrowed to FLT4S unless datatype = "FLT4S" asks for it (it rounds them to single precision).

    A datatype given is used as it is. An integer type needs whole numbers inside its range, else the write aborts.

  • NoData (nodata). One value marks the missing cells of all layers. Cells that hold this value are missing when read back; this is how a map whose 0 means "outside the map" is written (nodata = 0). With nodata = NULL, the first rule that applies:

    1. A flag set in the session on a raster read from files (terra::NAflag(x) <- ). On a raster in memory terra applies the flag at once, the cells become missing, and no flag is left: the rules below then apply.

    2. The NoData tag of the source file. It is not used for a layer with a scale or an offset, whose values are not the stored numbers the tag refers to.

    3. For an integer type chosen from the values (rule 2 of "Data type"), the default of the type: 255 for INT1U, 65535 for INT2U, -32768 for INT2S, 4294967295 for INT4U, -2147483648 for INT4S. The type is chosen so that no cell holds that value: values up to 254 fit INT1U, and with 255 among them the type is INT2U.

    4. For an integer type kept from the source or given with datatype, the same default, but only when cells are missing (found by one pass over the cells, made only in this case). The write aborts when a cell holds that value; give nodata then. Without missing cells the file has no NoData value: a Byte file without a tag whose 0 means "outside the map" gets none unless nodata = 0 is given.

    5. A float type has none: its missing cells are NaN.

    Layers whose flags or tags differ abort and ask for nodata. A nodata that the data type cannot hold aborts.

  • Creation options (gdal). The defaults suit reads from a bucket: COMPRESS=DEFLATE, PREDICTOR=2 (integer types) or PREDICTOR=3 (float types), BLOCKSIZE=512, BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER, and overviews built anew, never copied from a source file (OVERVIEWS=IGNORE_EXISTING), with OVERVIEW_RESAMPLING=NEAREST (integer types) or AVERAGE (float types). gdal is a character vector of KEY=VALUE options of GDAL's COG driver, e.g. gdal = c("COMPRESS=ZSTD", "LEVEL=9"): a key that has a default replaces it, other keys are added. Keys are compared in upper case, a key given twice aborts, and the order given does not change the file. The options are kept in the file, not in the catalog.

  • Legend of a class map. A categorical layer is one with a category table, set with levels(x) <- data.frame(value = , label = ): the codes in the first column, their labels in the second. levels<- renames the layer to the label column, so set names(x) after it. The codes are written to the file; the legend is recorded as values (the codes, sorted), levels (their labels) and levels_name (the name of the label column). Codes must be whole numbers and every code needs a label, else the write aborts. Of a category table with several label columns, only the active one (terra::activeCat()) is kept; the others are dropped, with a message.

  • Colours. The colour table of a layer, set with terra::coltab(x) <- data.frame(value = , col = ), is recorded as color_values (the codes, sorted) and colors (#RRGGBBAA). With a legend, only the colours of the legend's codes are kept. Without a legend every row of the colour table is kept; a colour table read from a file has 256 rows (the codes 0 to 255; a code without a colour is black, or transparent when it is the file's NoData value), and all 256 are recorded. Colours come from the raster only: a style file such as a QGIS .qml is not read.

  • Not stored. The time and the units of layers (terra::time(), terra::units()), and the columns of a category table other than the codes and the active labels. The file is written without categories, colour table, time and units; x itself is never changed. Only other metadata that a source file holds itself may be copied with it when GDAL copies the file (next point).

  • Two ways to write, and the room they need. The file is first written on the local disk, in the staging folder getOption("rcs.staging_dir") (default tempdir()), and then uploaded. Every temporary file lies below that folder.

    • A raster opened with terra::rast(file) and not changed in the session is copied by GDAL straight from its file, with no intermediate file. On a simulated map of 25,000 x 25,000 cells the staging folder held at most about 1.4 times the size of the output. "Not changed" means: all layers of one file in their order, with the file's layer names, extent and CRS, and no NoData flag or tag other than the value written. Setting a legend (and the layer name again) or colours is not a change. A file with a scale or an offset is not copied by GDAL.

    • Any other raster is written by terra: one in memory, computed, cropped, renamed, a subset of the layers, from several files, with a scale or an offset, or with another CRS or NoData value than its file. For a large raster terra first writes an intermediate file; on the same map the staging folder then held about 3.6 times the size of the output. A raster held in memory also needs RAM for all its cells, so write a large map from its file.

    For a raster read from files, the write warns (class rcs_warning_staging_space) when the drive of the staging folder has less free room than twice the size of the source files, and goes on. The ps package tells the free room; without it, and for a raster in memory, there is no check. options(rcs.staging_dir = ) moves the staging to another drive.

The same raster written with the same arguments gives the same file and the same version. The legend, the colours, the time and the units do not change the file: the same cells with and without them give the same version, and only the catalog entry differs. Writing the same cells with another legend or other colours keeps the version, sends no file and replaces the legend and the colours recorded for that version; the earlier ones are not kept. A datatype, nodata or gdal gives another file and another version only when it changes the file: nodata = 0 for a source file already tagged 0, or an option equal to its default, gives the same one. The two ways of writing may give different bytes for the same cells. A raster written with a version of the package before 0.0.0.9005 gets a new version when it is written again, even with unchanged cells: the bytes of the file differ.

DuckDB input

x may be a lazy table on a DuckDB connection (from dplyr::tbl(), for example on a view of store_duckdb(), or from store_open(engine = "duckdb")), so that a result computed in DuckDB is stored without being collected into R as a whole.

  • A table (no geometry column) with a partition is written one partition at a time. The query runs as a subquery 2 + P times (P partitions): once to check the key, once for the partition values and row counts, then once per partition, whose rows are copied into the temporary table rcs_write_<random>_part, written, checked and dropped. DuckDB then needs room for about the largest partition, not for the whole result. The query must therefore be deterministic (give the same rows each time), and is best a scan of stored files or views; an expensive query is better computed once into a DuckDB table first. options(rcs.duckdb_stream = FALSE) turns this off.

  • Otherwise (no partition, geospatial data, or rcs.duckdb_stream = FALSE) the query runs once into a temporary copy, the table rcs_write_<random> on the same connection, which every later step reads; the copy needs room for the whole result in DuckDB's memory or its temporary folder.

The temporary tables are dropped when the call ends, also after an error. The key and the partitions are checked in DuckDB, and the rows are fetched in batches of getOption("rcs.duckdb_batch_rows") rows (default 5e5), so that R holds about one batch at a time; a progress bar shows the batches unless options(rcs.quiet = TRUE). For the duration of the call the connection runs with preserve_insertion_order = true, so that the rows reach R in the order the write asks for; the caller's setting is restored when the call ends, also after an error. DuckDB never uploads: the files are staged and land in every location as for any other write. Staged files need free room equal to the output in getOption("rcs.staging_dir") (default tempdir()); setting it to a folder on the store's drive avoids copying them across drives. The files equal those written from the same rows collected into R, so both give the same version.

  • Modes "create" and "replace" only; "update" aborts (collect the rows and update from R, or write the whole dataset).

  • Columns .rcs_id, h3, bbox and geom are the package's own: they are dropped with a message and computed again. Columns h3_p<r> are user columns.

  • Types: integer, double, VARCHAR, DATE and BOOLEAN are stored as they are; BIGINT is stored as 64-bit integers read back as bit64::integer64; TIMESTAMP is stored without time zone (its wall clock) and TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE in UTC. HUGEINT, UHUGEINT, INTERVAL, UNION and MAP columns abort, naming them; cast them in the query. DuckDB's sum() of an integer column is a HUGEINT: write as.integer(sum(x)) or as.numeric(sum(x)) in dbplyr. Values keep their storage types: a factor read through a view is VARCHAR and is stored as text.

  • Geospatial data: a column geometry holding WKB (BLOB, as in views in arrow mode) or of type GEOMETRY (as in native views) makes the dataset geospatial, and crs is then required. The geometries pass through R in batches: for each batch the bounding boxes, the H3 cells and the index rows are computed as for an sf object (with geocode_engine, and the warning of "Geocoding engines") and kept in the staging folder; the rows are then sorted by cell and written from DuckDB. partition = "h3" and geocode = FALSE work as for an sf object.

  • Lazy tables on other databases abort: collect them first.

Geocoding engines

A geospatial row whose geometry lies inside one H3 cell gets that cell. For a row that crosses cell edges, the package computes the cells it touches and the share of the row in each; h3 is the cell of the largest share, and every touched cell goes to the index table. geocode_engine says how these cells are computed:

  • "auto" (the default): each such row is checked on the sphere (s2). A valid row is geocoded on the sphere. An invalid one (for example valid in the plane, but with a duplicated vertex or a spike that s2 rejects) is rebuilt by s2; when the rebuilt copy is empty or does not keep its area (length for lines) within getOption("rcs.s2_rebuild_tol") (default 1e-3), the row is geocoded in the plane instead.

  • "s2": on the sphere; invalid rows are rebuilt by s2 (geocoded in the plane when the rebuild fails).

  • "planar": every crossing row in the plane of the coordinates (slower).

Rows whose box spans 180 degrees of longitude or more are geocoded on the sphere with every engine. Rebuilt geometries are used only for the cells; the stored geometry is unchanged. One warning per write (class rcs_warning_s2_rebuild) counts the rows rebuilt and those geocoded in the plane, and names the first five of each by key (or .rcs_id). The engine is recorded with the dataset, and the exact test of store_read() and store_intersects() follows it by default (exact_engine). The same input always gives the same cells, shares and version. Data in a projected CRS are geocoded from a copy in EPSG:4326.

Modes

  • "create": the dataset must not exist yet.

  • "replace": the whole dataset is replaced by x; columns, key, partitioning and kind may change. A dataset that does not exist yet is created.

  • "update": for partitioned datasets only. The partitions whose values occur in x are replaced entirely by the rows of x; the other partitions are kept; new values add partitions. The columns and their types must equal the stored ones, and the key must stay unique across the whole dataset. A message lists every replaced partition with its old and new number of rows: rows of a replaced partition that are missing from x disappear. In this mode key, partition, h3_res, geocode and geocode_engine come from the stored dataset; arguments that disagree abort. partition may be left out; if given, it must be what was given on create: "h3", or the column names. Partition columns given by the user, even ones named h3_p<r>, are kept as given: never recomputed from the geometries. With partition = "h3", an update that would need more than max_files files re-partitions the whole dataset at a coarser H3 resolution.

Writing the same data again gives the same version: the call reports the dataset as unchanged, uploads nothing to the primary, and only brings secondary locations that differ up to date.

History

Whether the replaced version is kept is decided by the dataset's own setting (history, recorded in its catalog entry), else by the connection's (store_connect(history = )), else by the store's default (store_create()). Without history, the files of the replaced version are deleted right after the catalogs are switched; with history, they stay until store_prune() removes them.

Failures

Every transfer is tried up to three times. If the primary fails before its catalog is switched, the call aborts and no catalog has changed; uploaded files are reused when the call is repeated (and removed by store_prune() otherwise). If a secondary fails, the call warns, continues with the next location and reports the secondary as behind; store_sync() repairs it.

See also

store_check(), store_history(), store_prune(), rcs_geo_add(), store_duckdb().

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-write")
st <- store_connect(
  file.path(root, "primary"),
  secondary = file.path(root, "copy"),
  create = TRUE
)
sales <- rcs_sim_table(200, seed = 1)
store_write(st, sales, "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 200 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary  2/2
#>   files sent  27.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy     2/2
#>   files sent  27.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 2 locations. Catalogs updated.

# The same data again: nothing is uploaded
store_write(st, sales, "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year",
  mode = "replace"
)
#> ℹ "sales/daily" is unchanged (version 41ec22ed5b5602ce): 200 rows in 2 files
#>   (partition year).
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary  unchanged
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy     up
#>   to date
#> ✔ All 2 locations hold this version.

# Replace one year
year_2024 <- sales[sales$year == 2024, ]
year_2024$qty <- year_2024$qty + 1L
store_write(st, year_2024, "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  mode = "update"
)
#> ℹ Updating "sales/daily": 1 partition replaced, 0 added, 1 kept.
#> • year = 2024: 97 rows -> 97 rows
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 200 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary  1/2
#>   files sent  13.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy     1/2
#>   files sent  13.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 2 locations. Catalogs updated.
st
#> ── rcs store ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Locations:
#>   primary      local  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary
#>   secondary 1  local  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy
#> History: off (store default)
#> Datasets: 1
#>   name     kind   rows     size  files  updated           1
#>   sales/
#>     daily  table   200  27.9 kB      2  2026-11-27 13:56  =
#> Secondary copies: = same, ≠ differs, – missing, ? unavailable.

# A class map: the codes go into the file, the legend and the colours
# into the catalog. `nodata = 0`: cells holding 0 are outside the map.
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cover <- terra::as.int(rcs_sim_raster(nrow = 60, ncol = 80)[["cover"]])
  cover[1:2, ] <- 0L
  levels(cover) <- data.frame(
    value = 1:5,
    label = c("water", "forest", "crop", "grass", "bare")
  )
  names(cover) <- "cover" # `levels<-` renamed the layer
  terra::coltab(cover) <- data.frame(
    value = 1:5,
    col = c("#1F78B4", "#33A02C", "#FFD92F", "#B2DF8A", "#B15928")
  )
  store_write(st, cover, "grids/cover",
    title = "Land cover", description = "A simulated class map.",
    nodata = 0
  )
  # One byte per cell, the NoData value and the number of classes
  print(store_describe(st, "grids/cover")$columns)

  # A large map is best written straight from its file: the data type
  # and the NoData tag of the file are kept. `gdal` changes the
  # compression here.
  file <- file.path(root, "cover.tif")
  terra::writeRaster(cover, file, datatype = "INT1U", NAflag = 0)
  store_write(st, terra::rast(file), "grids/cover_zstd",
    title = "Land cover, ZSTD", description = "A simulated class map.",
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=ZSTD", "LEVEL=9")
  )
  # The label column is named `cover` here, not `label`:
  # `terra::writeRaster()` named it after the layer
  print(terra::levels(store_read(st, "grids/cover_zstd"))[[1]])
}
#> ℹ Writing "grids/cover": 4,800 cells in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary  1/1
#>   files sent  1.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy     1/1
#>   files sent  1.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 2 locations. Catalogs updated.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   name  type  r_type                                            description
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>                                             <chr>      
#> 1 cover INT1U raster layer (60 x 80 cells, nodata 0, 5 classes) NA         
#> ℹ Writing "grids/cover_zstd": 4,800 cells in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/primary  1/1
#>   files sent  1.6 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-write/copy     1/1
#>   files sent  1.6 kB  0.1s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 2 locations. Catalogs updated.
#>   value  cover
#> 1     1  water
#> 2     2 forest
#> 3     3   crop
#> 4     4  grass
#> 5     5   bare
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
